newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana checks samples from Canadian gold find.
newsitem.headline: Ghana checks samples from Canadian gold find.

text.p: Ghana has ordered an independent check of gold samples from a potentially large discovery by a Canadian group prospecting at Stenpad, southwest of Kumasi.
"Whenever companies come up with results that suggest something else than our general geological survey, we want an independent opinion," said a Ghana Minerals Commission official.
"We are now trying to get some independent samples analysed," finance officer Ben Aryee told Reuters, adding that results could be expected by May before an announcement.
A joint venture by Golden Rule Resources Ltd and Hixon Gold Resources said in January samples taken from a 100m trench at Stedpad, 65 km west of Obuasi, showed an average of 8.75 grammes/tonne (g/t).
A first sample from the site, contained 20.91 g/t while the last had 19.02, it said.
In November, the group said samples from a 100m trench contained 7.3, 16.0, 27.5 and 54.4 g/t of gold.
"(Checks) happen every now and then," said Ayree.
Golden Rule is listed on the Toronto Stock exchange, Hixon on the Vancouver exchange.
Ghana's Minerals Commission was set up in 1986 to give policy advice on exploration and exploitation, attract foreign investors and negotiate leases, and review public agreements.
